short: The short written explanation attached to an accounting entry saying what it was for.
seoTitle: Narration in Accounting — Meaning and Examples
metaDescription: A narration is the short note on an accounting entry saying what the transaction was for. Why a good one saves hours at audit, with weak and strong examples.
definition: A narration is the short written explanation recorded against an accounting entry — a line saying what the transaction actually was, who it involved and which document supports it — so that the entry can be understood later without asking the person who made it.
bodyHtml:
Why it is not optional housekeeping

An amount and an account name tell you almost nothing a year later. The narration is what turns a ledger into something a new bookkeeper, a lender or an auditor can read without a conversation, and it is where most of the time in a catch-up or an audit is actually lost.

A weak narration and a good one

  • Weak: Payment made
  • Weak: Expenses
  • Good: Rent for September 2026, Shop 4, paid by NEFT to Mehta Properties, ref 4471
  • Good: Purchase invoice PI-233 from Kumar Traders, 40 kg flour, GST 5%

What a good narration contains

The period or date the transaction relates to, the other party by name, the document number, and anything unusual about it. Keep the pattern the same across the book — consistency is what makes a ledger searchable, and a searchable ledger is the difference between a two-hour close and a two-day one.

faq.question: How long should a narration be?
faq.answer: One line that answers what, who and which document. Longer than that and people stop reading it; shorter and it stops being useful.

faq.question: Does a narration matter if the bill is attached?
faq.answer: Yes, because you search the ledger before you open the attachment. The narration is the index; the bill is the evidence.
